key_insight: Distributed quantum computing requires online decisions about when to launch arriving circuits and where to place their qubits, without knowing future workloads.
engineering_relevance: Quantum-network schedulers must balance latency and throughput while respecting finite memory, probabilistic entanglement generation, decoherence, and competing jobs.
method: Formalize online scheduling and distribution of circuits across networked quantum processors.
At each arrival or completion, select waiting circuits to launch and assign their qubits.
Account for in-flight congestion and physical constraints while minimizing mean completion time and makespan.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes the problem formulation and objectives but reports no datasets, experimental results, or quantitative performance gains.
watch_item: Practical performance remains unverified in the abstract, particularly under variable arrival loads and stochastic entanglement generation.
paper_title: Online Scheduling and Distribution of Quantum Circuits over Quantum Networks
